Historical literacy tests were instruments of racial disenfranchisement
(administered arbitrarily, secretly graded, at the discretion of hostile
officials). The paper argues the design's safeguards are what separate it
from that history. If you believe they don't, tell us which one fails.

**Which safeguard do you believe fails (or is insufficient)?**

- [ ] Open, published item banks (no secret or discretionary testing)
- [ ] Adversarial authorship review (item writers counter-briefed)
- [ ] Random audits with mismatch penalties (items validated against outcomes)
- [ ] Sunset clauses / mandatory re-certification (standing decays)
- [ ] Universal democratic veto (supermajority can overturn any tier decision)
